sample2

sample2.Rd

Randomly sample elements from an object x, with a corrected behavior when x is made of a single element (see the details below).

Usage

sample2(
  x,
  size = NULL,
  replace = FALSE,
  prob = NULL,
  set_seed = NULL,
  safer_check = TRUE,
  lib_path = NULL,
  error_text = ""
)

Arguments

x

Object from which to sample elements. Any object that has a length (see length) and that can be subsetted using the [ operator (vector, factor, matrix, data frame, table, list, etc.).

size

Either NULL (default), meaning that all the elements of x are sampled exactly once (like in sample when x is not made of a single element), or a single non negative integer (integers of type double are accepted when they have a 0 modulo, i.e., 2.0 is accepted like 2L, but 2.5 is not). Sampling without replacement more elements than the length of x returns an error, like in sample.

replace

Single logical value. Should sampling be with replacement?

prob

Either NULL (default) or a vector of numeric probability weights of the same length as x. No negative, infinite, NA or factor value allowed (unlike sample, which accepts a factor).

set_seed

Either NULL (default) or a single positive or negative integer (integers of type double are accepted when they have a 0 modulo) used in base::set.seed() before sampling. Warning: unlike base::set.seed() called in the global environment, the .Random.seed object of the user global environment is restored at the end of the function execution (the random generator state existing before the function call), so that the function does not modify the random generator state of the user. If NULL, the current random generator state of the user is directly used and modified, like in sample.

safer_check

Single logical value. Perform some "safer" checks? If TRUE, checkings are performed before main code running (see the safer-r project): 1) correct lib_path argument value 2) required functions and related packages effectively present in local R libraries and 3) R classical operators (like "<-") not overwritten by another package because of the R scope. Must be set to FALSE if this function is used inside another "safer" function to avoid pointless multiple checkings.

lib_path

Vector of characters specifying the absolute pathways of the directories containing the required packages for the function, if not in the default directories. Useful when R packages are not installed in the default directories because of lack of admin rights. More precisely, lib_path is passed through the new argument of .libPaths() so that the new library paths are unique(c(new, .Library.site, .Library)). Warning: .libPaths() is restored to the initial paths, after function execution. Ignored if NULL (default) or if the safer_check argument is FALSE: only the pathways specified by the current .libPaths() are used for package calling.

error_text

Single character string used to add information in error messages returned by the function, notably if the function is inside other functions, which is practical for debugging. Example: error_text = " INSIDE <PACKAGE_1>::<FUNCTION_1> INSIDE <PACKAGE_2>::<FUNCTION_2>.". If NULL, converted into "". Of note, in arg_check(), error_text is also used at the end of the string returned when no problem is detected.

Value

The sampled elements, with the subsetting semantics of the [ operator, i.e., the same class as x, with the dimensions possibly dropped like in sample (for instance, sampling a matrix returns a vector).

Details

The sample function behaves in a confusing way when x is made of a single positive numeric value: base::sample(x = 4, size = 3, replace = TRUE) draws 3 values between 1 and 4 (the single value 4 is used as the size of the population 1:4), and base::sample(x = 4, size = 3, replace = FALSE) returns 3 distinct values between 1 and 4 without error, although a single value cannot be sampled 3 times without replacement. sample2() corrects these behaviors: the single value is used as the population itself, made of this single element. Thus, sample2(x = 4, size = 3, replace = TRUE) returns 4 4 4, and sample2(x = 4, size = 3, replace = FALSE) returns an error because the single value 4 cannot be sampled 3 times without replacement. Note that this also implies sample2(x = 4) (i.e., with size = NULL) returns the single value 4, unlike base::sample(x = 4) which draws 4 values between 1 and 4. For any other x value (length superior to 1, or length 1 but not made of a positive numeric value), sample2() behaves exactly like sample.

Examples

# Warning: these examples may not work well when using the "Run examples" link
# because of a particular environment. Please, copy-paste in a local environment.
# See also https://safer-r.github.io/saferTool/articles/sample2.html
vec <- c(1:5) ; sample2(x = vec, size = 3, set_seed = 1)
#> [1] 1 4 3

sample2(x = 4, size = 3, replace = TRUE, set_seed = 1) # 4 4 4 (see the details below)
#> [1] 4 4 4

# This example returns an error: the single value 4 cannot be sampled 3 times without replacement
# sample2(x = 4, size = 3, replace = FALSE)

# This example returns an error because of the negative probability
# sample2(x = c(1:5), size = 3, replace = TRUE, prob = c(-1, 1, 1, 1, 1))
